newsitem.title: FRANCE: Economic highlights of French RPR-UDF manifesto.
newsitem.headline: Economic highlights of French RPR-UDF manifesto.

text.p: The French ruling centre-right RPR-UDF coalition's manifesto released on Tuesday for the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election includes the following economic points:

- Commitment to France joining European single currency as scheduled on January 1, 1999 in order to stimulate economic growth and employment. Enlargement of European Union to central and eastern European countries after reform of its institutions
- Stabilise public spending to make sure that it does not rise faster than inflation
- Continue reduction of income tax and lower local business taxes with aim of cutting unemployment (now at record 12.8 percent)
- Reduce burden of employer's social security and other charges in low-wage sector in exchange for job creation
- Free up entrepreneurial initiative in interests of job creation
- Creation of "a modern state" that serves citizens better and is focused on the main tasks of government
- Overhauling welfare state in order to better protect it. Commitment to French social welfare model, reimbursement of medical costs, free choice of doctors by patients
- Commitment to maintenance of minimum unemployment benefit (RMI)
- More emphasis on apprenticeships and technology training to prepare students for working world
- Creation of savings plan "Livret Emploi" (jobs passbook) to steer individual savings toward small and medium sized businesses.
- Reduction "by two-thirds" in official paperwork which small businesses have to complete
- Urge trade unions and business to negotiate on working hours to spur job creation
- Increase age limit for receipt of family allowances
- Encourage all work time formats, including flexible hours, to make it easier for people to look after their families
- Commitment to defend French commercial interests internationally, with particular emphasis on agricultural matters
- Create a Europe that avoids unfair competition among member states
